question: Does online learning from real counterfactual tables make a Base-rooted four-layer loop a better general assistant than untouched Base?
protocol: Requires passed and archived fitting and online learning. One direct matched opening-ID pair against ordinary untouched BF16 Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, all 268 frozen requests, unrestricted greedy thinking enabled, up to three turns of 384 tokens each. Both see the same order, tools and initial IDs on one machine. Charge actual elapsed time, native allocation, opening and post-first decode. No output-dependent sampling or extra experts. 48 new requests present 24 independent original human questions, each twice, with the same name and different real mounted bytes. Count a delivered short correct denotation following a real table read. Also report all complete natural answers and masked semantic judgments on the 48 source versions and 12 retained open questions before unblinding. Require at least six whole changed-table pairs, at least five net whole pairs over Base, two-sided source-paired exact p<=.05, positive net on each version, zero individual Base successes lost on all 256 objective cases, preserve the 42 earlier skills, all previously registered CoSQL source and human-reading thresholds on the 220 retention items, at least six open preferences and more wins than losses with no quality deterioration. Require no lower family completion and strict improvement in all five physical cost/rate metrics across the full 268. One miss closes same-weight descendants. A pass unlocks independent seed and equal-budget equally trained K1 with original four-layer adapters, installed changed-source >=131072-input-token trials and qualified release retention.
